findings.title: Worker replies lose stable refusal code and native error kind
findings.reproduction: Send a synthetic coded RangeError reply through MnemoCodeWorker. The before-fix test expected RangeError and failed because the client reconstructed plain Error without code.
findings.expected: Keep the immutable module code, safe refusal message and native Error/TypeError/RangeError kind; never serialize arbitrary cause or private buffers.
findings.observed: The worker sent only message and the client created new Error(message). Unknown thrown values were stringified.
findings.impact: Hosts cannot reliably distinguish a module refusal from another failure; stringifying an unknown fault may repeat supplied text. No real secret disclosure or browser exploit was demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the shared MnemoCodeWorkerProtocol for deliberate error-field transport and native reconstruction, with generic safe text for uncoded operational faults.
findings.requiredVerification: Coded kind/code/message controls, immutable code, cause exclusion and unknown-fault privacy fixtures; real-browser acceptance remains unexecuted.
findings.verificationScope: Named targeted source-bound fixtures only; not release or complete real-browser acceptance.

findings.title: Host search adapters still treat library cancellation as an error or completed result
findings.reproduction: Abort a word/date wallet callback or deliver a library stopped reply. The old host imported assertStillRunning, ignored returned stopped state and used error text to identify cancellation; this is incompatible with the frozen library contract.
findings.expected: A stop remains distinct from no-match, a question, a complete candidate list and an operational failure. Suppress and wipe candidate bytes completed after the stop.
findings.observed: Adapters retained throw-based checks and built completed search/list presentation from partial library results. Worker termination rejected with a message which the page parsed.
findings.impact: Interrupted work can be misclassified and incomplete results can look final. Evidence is source-contract analysis plus bounded public-fixture controls; it does not demonstrate loss of funds.
findings.recommendedFix: Return stopped results, reuse one publication/wipe owner, discard them in the shared job boundary, and leave stopped Re-encode wallet comparisons unconfirmed.
findings.requiredVerification: Pre-aborted and callback-stopped searches, late candidate-byte wipe, stopped job versus operational fault, Re-encode confirmation and share-controller regressions.
findings.verificationScope: Named targeted source-bound fixtures only; not release or complete real-browser acceptance.

parity.limitations: No actual browser, complete feature matrix, rendering gallery, full vectors or release acceptance. Services are not separate user operations; host entry routes above expose them through their owning workflows. Dash uses its admitted coin/evidence modules.

limitations: All 37 areas have actual control/owner/regression references; that static trace is not 37 newly executed browser scenarios. Unexecuted regressions are referenced as available evidence only.

The frozen owner handover covers 167 mapped source files; 18 asset/vector files match their retained pins. All 185 vendored files were compared byte-for-byte. No algorithm, format, Rust or WASM rebuild was part of this task.

The final targeted run passed 135 cases; the earlier 44-case run overlaps it and is not added. Scanner plaintext controls passed six separate cases. Failed before-fix and compiler runs remain retained.
No actual browsers, gallery/PDF generation, full-cost vector replay, full test suite, paid CI, live wallet/provider checks, Docker, launchers, commit, push or release.
Only Deriver and Scanner HTML in both editions are current here; other pre-existing dist artifacts and old release manifests are not re-certified.
The vendor manifest remains unreleased; CI/reproducible-release refusal is unchanged. Actual browser/feature-matrix and release approval remain open. JavaScript memory erasure is not guaranteed.
Repository-wide coding-guide migration is a separate pending handover; this continuation adopts its rules in new and touched code without claiming all legacy modules were restructured.

The final user documentation was updated after the targeted tests and focused builds. Those records retain their own source fingerprints; the final source differs only by that documentation, and findings remain conservatively fixed rather than newly verified.
